body: Morningstar 2025: 8.7% vs 9.9% (1.2 pts/yr; 2.1 for volatile funds). India Axis MF 2003–22: funds 19.1% vs investors 13.8%. DALBAR noisy (848 bp 2024 vs 72 bp 2025).
title: Behavior gap: investors earn less than their funds

body: Status on 19 Nov 2026 versus each stock's all-time high: 8 of 27 are ≥50% below (Symphony −74, KPIT −72, La Opala −66, Tata Elxsi −64, Alkyl −64, Kaynes −62, Cochin −60, Avanti −52); 5 more are 40–50% below (Deepak −50, Astral −48, Mazagon −47, Page −42, Trent −41); Suzlon is −56% from its 2024 turnaround peak. Still near highs (≤15% off): Eicher, Bajaj Finance, APL Apollo, Pidilite, Titan, BSE, HAL, BEL. Five ending mechanisms: (a) growth deceleration at a premium multiple (Page, Astral, Tata Elxsi, Trent, Symphony, La Opala, KPIT, Dixon); (b) commodity or spread reversal (Deepak, Alkyl, Avanti, Balkrishna's ROCE fall); (c) narrative timing slip (shipyards' P75(I) award); (d) earnings miss plus governance or disclosure question (Kaynes); (e) customer or regional concentration shock (KPIT on BMW and Europe, Tata Elxsi on JLR and autos, Avanti on US shrimp). The survivors share continuing double-digit EPS growth and a P/E that normalised gradually rather than being at a peak. Lesson: multibaggers are rentals more often than lifetime holdings. Define in advance the specific driver whose break means exit (LFL, spread, award, client), and track it quarterly.
title: How Indian multibagger runs end: 13 of 27 are ≥40% below peak in Nov 2026
